cards.title: It sounds just like them
cards.body:
Your phone rings. It's your cousin's voice, upset: "I'm in trouble. I need money right now. Please don't tell anyone."

It sounds exactly like them. But it might not be them at all. Some scammers now use AI to copy people's voices and faces. This lesson shows you how to stay calm and check.

cards.title: Fake voices and faces
cards.body:
AI can learn how a person looks and sounds from real recordings, sometimes from just a few seconds of a video posted online. Then it can make **new** audio or video of them saying things they never said.

A fake video or picture made like this is called a **deepfake**. A fake copy of someone's voice is called a **voice clone**. They can be very convincing, so you can't always tell by looking or listening.

cards.title: The same old tricks
cards.body:
Deepfake scams use the same tricks as every scam:

- **Hurry:** you must act right now, so you don't stop to check.
- **Keep it secret:** don't tell anyone, so nobody can warn you.
- **Money, gift cards or codes:** because they're hard to get back once sent.
- **A new number or account:** "I lost my phone, this is my new number", so you can't call the real person.

**What to do:** hang up or stop replying. Then contact the person on the number or account **you already have** for them, or ask a trusted adult to check. The voice or face might be fake, but these red flags are real.

items.label: Don't tell Mum, just send it
Buy gift cards and send the codes
It's me, I've got a new number
Send it in the next 5 minutes!
See you at practice on Saturday
Can you bring my jumper home?

cards.hint: Look for the four tricks: hurry, secrets, money or codes, and a new number.
cards.nudge: Check each message for pressure to hurry, to keep a secret, to send money or codes, or a new number.
cards.explanation: Rushing you, asking for **secrets**, **gift cards or codes**, and a **new number** are all red flags, whoever the message seems to be from. Plans, favours and birthday wishes are normal.

cards.prompt: Your phone rings from a number you don't know.

steps.text: It sounds exactly like your grandma: "I've lost my purse and I'm stuck. Please send me money now, and don't worry your parents." What do you do?

choices.text: Send the money: it's her voice
choices.consequence: Voices can be copied with AI. Money sent to a scammer is usually gone for good.

choices.text: Say you'll call her back, and hang up
choices.consequence: Good: hanging up stops the pressure. Now check.

choices.text: Keep chatting to find out more
choices.consequence: Scammers are good at talking. The longer you stay on, the more they can pressure you. It's safer to hang up.

choices.text: Call Grandma on the number you already have
choices.consequence: She answers at home, perfectly fine. It was a scam, and you stopped it.

choices.text: Call back the number that just rang
choices.consequence: That number belongs to the scammer, so they'd just answer again. Use the number you already know.

choices.text: Tell a trusted adult what happened
choices.consequence: Good choice: an adult can call Grandma on her real number with you, and help report the scam.

cards.hint: Spot the red flags first: a new number, hurry, secrecy and money. Then remember the card about what to do.
cards.explanation: A new number, **hurry**, **money** and **keep it from your parents** are all red flags. Hang up, then check using the number **you already have**, or with a **trusted adult**. Never call back the number that rang you.

cards.title: Ask something only they'd know
cards.body:
Another way to check: ask a question only the real person could answer, like the name of your first pet. Some families agree a **code word** together, just for emergencies, and never post it online.

If the caller can't answer, or gets cross and keeps rushing you, hang up.

cards.prompt: A video call from your friend's account asks you to send a code that just arrived by text. Their face and voice look right. What's the **best** thing to do?

options.text: Don't send it. Check with your friend another way, like their usual number
Send it: you can see their face
options.nudge: Faces can be faked with AI. The request for a code is the red flag. How else could you reach your friend?

options.text: Send half of the code to be safe
options.nudge: Any part of a code can help a scammer. Is there a way to check it's really them first?
Posting doesn't tell you whether it's really your friend. How could you reach them directly?

cards.hint: A face and voice can be faked. What can't a scammer fake?
cards.explanation: A [[deepfake]] can copy a face and voice, but it can't answer on your friend's **usual number**. Asking for a code is a red flag, so don't send it: check another way first. Sign-in codes are never safe to share.

cards.title: If someone makes a fake of you
cards.body:
If someone makes or shares a fake picture or video of you, including a fake nude or sexual image:

- It's **not your fault**, and you won't be in trouble for asking for help.
- **Don't share it** any further, even to show someone. **Don't pay** or send anything they ask for.
- **Save evidence**: screenshot the messages, the account name and the web address, but never the image itself.
- **Tell a trusted adult**.
- **Report** it to the app, and to **eSafety** (esafety.gov.au/report), which can help get fake intimate images taken down. If you're under 18 and someone is threatening to share it, or asking you for sexual images or money, report it to the **ACCCE** too (accce.gov.au/report).

cards.prompt: Someone has shared a fake picture of you. Sort what to **do**, and what **not** to do.

items.label: Report it to the app and eSafety
Share it to show your friends
Save a copy of the image itself

cards.hint: Look back at the list on the last card: what helps you, and what helps whoever made the fake?
cards.nudge: Saving evidence means the messages and the account, not the picture. And you never have to deal with this alone.
cards.explanation: **Do:** tell a trusted adult, screenshot the messages and account, and report it. **Don't:** share it, save the image itself, pay, or keep it to yourself. None of this is your fault.

cards.prompt: A video message arrives from an account with your coach's name and face.

steps.text: "Send me a photo of you in your uniform for the team page. Keep it between us." It really looks like your coach. It could be a [[deepfake]]. What do you do?

choices.consequence: "Keep it between us" is a red flag, even from someone you know. A real coach wouldn't ask you to keep secrets.

choices.text: Don't reply, and tell a trusted adult
choices.consequence: Exactly. An adult can check with the real coach. Secrets and requests for photos are red flags, whatever face is on the screen.

choices.text: Ask them to send another video to prove it
choices.consequence: A deepfake can make another video. Check another way: through a trusted adult, or the coach's usual contact.

cards.hint: Look past the face. Which red flag is in the message itself?
cards.explanation: The face might be real or fake, but **"keep it between us"** is a red flag either way. Don't reply, and **tell a trusted adult**, who can check with the real coach. Another video proves nothing.

cards.prompt: Match each red flag to why scammers use it.

pairs.right: So you don't stop to check
So you can't call the real person

cards.hint: Each trick takes away one of your ways to stay safe. Which way does each one take away?
cards.nudge: Think about what each trick stops you doing: checking, getting help, reaching the real person, or getting money back.
cards.explanation: **Hurry** stops you checking; **secrets** stop anyone warning you; a **new number** stops you reaching the real person; and **gift cards and codes** are hard to get back. Spot the trick, and the scam falls apart.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- AI can copy voices and faces: **deepfakes** and **voice clones**. You can't always tell by looking or listening.
- The red flags still work: **hurry**, **secrets**, **money or codes**, a **new number**.
- Hang up, then check on the number you already have, ask something only they'd know, or tell a trusted adult.
- If someone fakes a picture of you: it's not your fault. Don't share it or pay; save evidence, tell a trusted adult, and report it to the app and eSafety.
